podcast.title: Death (May 1995)
podcast.body: Bradley Nowell, identified as "Brad Noel" and the singer of Sublime, died in May 1995 from a drug overdose. "Brad Noel, singer, sublime, Drug Overdose, May 1995."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Death by Heroin Overdose
podcast.body: Died of a heroin overdose on May 25, 1996, after taking a "celebratory hit of heroin." This occurred just six weeks before Sublime's highly anticipated major label third album was scheduled to be released. "But before they could join the ranks of bands like Green Day and the offspring, the singer up and died of an overdose. His name was Bradley Noelle."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Death as a Career Move ｜ From the Archives

podcast.title: Greater Posthumous Earnings
podcast.body: Bradley Nowell ultimately "made more money dead than he ever did alive" due to the massive commercial success of Sublime's albums and releases following his death. "Sublime, featuring singer Brad Noelle, a guy who's made more money dead than he ever did alive."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Band Formation and Early Gigs
xref.body: Sublime, featuring Bradley Nowell, Bud Gaugh, and Eric Wilson, began playing house parties in 1988, struggling to attract record labels due to their "punky Reggae band" style which was a hard sell at the time. "Sublime with Bud Gow and Eric Wilson started playing House Parties in 1988."

xref.title: Bradley Nowell's Cause of Death
xref.body: Paramedics were called to the scene but it was too late; Bradley Nowell had died several hours earlier and was pronounced dead at the scene at the age of 28. "Paramedics were called, but it was too late. Bradley had died several hours earlier and was pronounced dead on the scene."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Bradley Nowell's Death and Discovery
xref.body: Bradley Nowell was found dead on the floor of his motel room the next morning by his bandmates, with his beloved Dalmatian, Lou Dog, whining on the bed beside him. Initially, they thought he was merely too drunk to get into bed, but then they observed a yellow film around his mouth. "Later that morning, they went to Bradley's room and found him on the floor with Lou Dog whining on the bed."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Bradley Nowell's Early Life and Musical Influence
xref.body: Bradley Nowell experienced his parents' divorce, initially living with his mother before moving in with his father, who taught him guitar. During a sailing trip to the Virgin Islands with his father, Bradley was introduced to reggae, which he greatly loved. "Dad not only taught him how to play guitar, but the two of them also went sailing in the Virgin Islands where Bradley was introduced to Reggae."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Bradley Nowell's Heroin Use Justification
xref.body: Bradley Nowell developed a heavy heroin habit, believing that the drug helped him cope with and fulfill the demanding obligations of being a rock star. "At the same time though, Bradley fell into heroin use. He felt that the drug helped him live up to the obligations of being a rock star and he started using heavily."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Bradley Nowell's Last Night and Morning
xref.body: After a show in San Francisco on May 24, 1996, Bradley Nowell returned to the Ocean View Motel with his Dalmatian, Lou Dog. The next morning, he attempted to persuade his hungover bandmates to join him at the beach, but they chose to remain in bed. "After a show in San Francisco and made the 24th of 1996, everyone went back to the Ocean View Motel."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Bradley Nowell's Son Takes Over Vocals
xref.body: In 2024, Bradley Nowell's son, Jacob, assumed the role of lead vocalist for Sublime, continuing his father's legacy in the band. "In 2024, Bradley's son Jacob took over his lead vocalist."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Bradley Nowell's Tour Schedule Leading to Death
xref.body: In late May 1996, Sublime embarked on a tour that included dates in Northern California, planned subsequent swings through Europe, and a return for an American East Coast trek. "In late May 1996, Sublime was on a tour through Northern California, which was to be followed by a swing through Europe and then back for a trek up and down the American East Coast."
